Description: Mihrdat III reigned in 374 AD as King of Iberia (Kartli) in the central Caucasus, scion of the Christian Chosroid dynasty chronicled by Faustus of Byzantium. Governing the strategic Kura river valley and Caucasian Gate defiles, his kingdom stood as the primary buffer and geopolitical flashpoint between Rome and Sassanid Persia. A devout Christian monarch committed to the Nicene cross of Saint Nino, Mihrdat was backed by Emperor Valens, yet found his crown contested by Persian-backed pretenders. Following an imperial treaty partitioning Iberia along the river, Mihrdat governed the northern sector from fortified crag citadels. Commanding elite Georgian mountain archers and Azat noble cavalry, he guarded the northern defiles against Persian encroachments with tragic determination. During the tumultuous conflicts of the late fourth century, he served as an indispensable pillar of tactical stability and frontline command. Drilling his warrior retinues daily and inspecting ramparts, he personally verified spearheads, shield-bosses, and sentry postings, eliminating indiscipline through exemplary leadership. When battle was joined, his cold composure under fire directed devastating counter-thrusts that shattered hostile formations at critical junctures. Placing the preservation of his folk and territorial sovereignty above all mortal ambition, this dedicated warlord stood as an unbreakable bastion of defiance.

Motivations: Expel Sassanid client factions to reunite all of Iberia under the Christian Chosroid crown
Secure the Darial Gorge (Caucasian Gates) to prevent northern nomadic raids into Christian dioceses
Values: The Holy Cross and the Caucasian peaks are inviolable; we bow not to Zoroastrian fire-altars
A Christian monarch must shed his blood for his flock; surrendering sacred soil is mortal sin
Fears: Dreads sudden Roman legionary withdrawal abandoning his mountain kingdom to Sassanid armies
